$comment: Canned replies for the stand-in platform (demo/fake-platform.js in the case desk engine), so this desk can be tried with no platform. Each key is a distinctive part of a case title, matched without regard to case. The stand-in adds its own first line saying that the reply is canned. The suppliers and their answers are invented. Start the stand-in with DESK_CONFIG pointing at desk.config.json in this folder.

replies.Larkspur:
Summary
Larkspur Cloud Archive Ltd hosts the bank's document archive. Tier 1, because it holds customer information. Clause 1.3 applies: every requirement applies to a tier 1 supplier.

Draft assessment. For review by the third-party risk officer. Not issued.

| # | Requirement | Standard | Supplier's answer | Evidence relied on | Mark | Reason and what the officer should check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The supplier holds an independent security certification or audit report dated within the last 12 months. | MTB-STD-041 2.1 | Yes, holds an audit report | Independent security audit report dated 15 September 2025 | not met | The report is 14 months old at the case date of 16 November 2026. The limit is 12 months. Check whether a newer report exists. |
| 2 | Customer information is encrypted at rest and in transit. | MTB-STD-041 2.2 | Yes | Security overview: encrypted at rest and in transit on every system that holds customer information | met | The answer and the evidence match the requirement. |
| 3 | Multi-factor authentication is required for every member of the supplier's staff who can reach the bank's information. | MTB-STD-041 2.3 | Administrators only | Access policy: multi-factor authentication for administrator accounts, other staff sign in with a password | partly met | Covers the administrators but not the other staff. Check which other staff can reach the bank's information. |
| 4 | The supplier tells the bank of a security incident that affects the bank within 24 hours of detecting it. | MTB-STD-041 2.4 | Within 72 hours | Service terms 11.2: notice within 72 hours of detecting an incident | not met | 72 hours misses the limit of 24 hours. |
| 5 | A penetration test at least once a year, critical findings closed within 30 days. | MTB-STD-041 2.5 | Yearly test, critical findings closed in 45 days | Penetration test summary dated 20 May 2026: annual test, critical findings closed within 45 days | not met | The yearly test meets the requirement. 45 days misses the limit of 30 days, and a missed limit is not met. |
| 6 | Customer information stays in Meridia unless the bank has agreed otherwise in writing, backups included. | MTB-STD-041 3.1 | Archive in Meridia, backups in Quenmark | Hosting schedule: primary site Meridia, backup site Quenmark. No written agreement from the bank is attached | not met | Backups are outside Meridia and no written agreement from the bank is shown. |
| 7 | The supplier lists its sub-processors and tells the bank 30 days before a change. | MTB-STD-041 3.2 | Yes | Sub-processor list version 4 and service terms 9.1: 30 days' written notice | met | The answer and the evidence match the requirement. |
| 8 | Return or deletion of the bank's information within 60 days, with a certificate. | MTB-STD-041 3.3 | Deleted within 90 days | Service terms 20.3: deleted within 90 days of the end of the contract | not met | 90 days misses the limit of 60 days. No certificate is mentioned. |
| 9 | A business continuity plan tested within the last 12 months. | MTB-STD-041 4.1 | Tested on 16 March 2026 | Business continuity test report: full test on 16 March 2026, passed | met | The test is 8 months before the case date of 16 November 2026, within 12 months. |
| 10 | Recovery time objective no longer than four hours. | MTB-STD-041 4.2 | 8 hours | Service schedule: recovery time objective 8 hours | not met | 8 hours misses the limit of four hours. |
| 11 | Backups are tested at least twice a year. | MTB-STD-041 4.3 | Once a year | Backup procedure: test restore once a year | not met | Once a year misses the limit of twice a year. A missed frequency is not met. |
| 12 | The contract gives the bank the right to audit. | MTB-STD-041 5.1 | Yes | Contract 14.1: the customer may audit once a year on 30 days' notice | met | The answer and the evidence match the requirement. |
| 13 | An exit plan is agreed before the service starts. | MTB-STD-041 5.2 | After signing | Contract clause 18: an exit plan is to be agreed after signing | not met | The exit plan is not agreed before the service starts. The planned start is 1 March 2027 and no exit plan dated before it is shown. |
| 14 | The contract gives the bank the right to be told of sub-contracting. | MTB-STD-041 5.3 | Yes | Contract 9.2: the supplier will tell the customer of any sub-contracting | met | The answer and the evidence match the requirement. |
| 15 | Liability insurance of at least USD 5 million. | MTB-STD-041 5.4 | USD 2 million | Insurance certificate: liability limit USD 2,000,000 | not met | Below the minimum of USD 5 million. |
| 16 | Background check for staff who can reach customer information. | MTB-STD-041 6.1 | Yes | People procedure: every person who can reach customer information passes a background check before they start | met | The answer and the evidence match the requirement. |
| 17 | Security training at least once a year. | MTB-STD-041 6.2 | Yes, every year | Training record: completed by all staff on 9 March 2026, the course is run every year | met | The training is 8 months before the case date, within the year. |

Recommendation: do not recommend approval: requirements 2.1, 2.4, 2.5, 3.1, 3.3, 4.2, 4.3, 5.2 and 5.4 are not met. A tier 1 supplier is approved by the Risk Committee, not by the desk (MTB-STD-041 7.4). A requirement that is not met can be accepted only as a recorded exception approved by the Risk Committee, with an end date (7.5).
replies.Tessaly:
Summary
Tessaly Payment Gateway Services processes card payments for the bank. Tier 1, because its service is critical. Clause 1.3 applies: every requirement applies to a tier 1 supplier.

Draft assessment. For review by the third-party risk officer. Not issued.

| # | Requirement | Standard | Supplier's answer | Evidence relied on | Mark | Reason and what the officer should check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The supplier holds an independent security certification or audit report dated within the last 12 months. | MTB-STD-041 2.1 | Yes, holds an audit report | Independent security audit report dated 20 March 2026, unqualified | met | The report is 8 months old at the case date of 17 November 2026, within 12 months. |
| 2 | Customer information is encrypted at rest and in transit. | MTB-STD-041 2.2 | Yes | Security overview: all customer information is encrypted at rest and in transit, on every system that holds or moves it | met | The answer and the evidence match the requirement. |
| 3 | Multi-factor authentication is required for every member of the supplier's staff who can reach the bank's information. | MTB-STD-041 2.3 | Every member of staff who can reach a customer's environment | Access policy: required for every member of staff with access to customer environments, on site or remote | met | Covers all staff by any route. |
| 4 | The supplier tells the bank of a security incident that affects the bank within 24 hours of detecting it. | MTB-STD-041 2.4 | Within 12 hours | Contract schedule 3, clause 2: notice within 12 hours of detecting an incident | met | 12 hours is within the limit of 24 hours. |
| 5 | A penetration test at least once a year, critical findings closed within 30 days. | MTB-STD-041 2.5 | Yearly test, critical findings closed in 14 days | Penetration test summary dated 12 August 2026: annual test, critical findings closed within 14 days | met | The test is within the year and 14 days is within the limit of 30 days. |
| 6 | Customer information stays in Meridia unless the bank has agreed otherwise in writing, backups included. | MTB-STD-041 3.1 | Meridia only, backups included | Hosting schedule: primary and backup sites in Meridia, nothing held outside it | met | The answer and the evidence match the requirement. |
| 7 | The supplier lists its sub-processors and tells the bank 30 days before a change. | MTB-STD-041 3.2 | Yes, 45 days' notice | Sub-processor list version 7 and contract 9.1: 45 days' written notice | met | 45 days is longer than the 30 days required. |
| 8 | Return or deletion of the bank's information within 60 days, with a certificate. | MTB-STD-041 3.3 | Within 30 days, with a certificate | Contract 21.2: returned or deleted within 30 days, with a signed certificate | met | 30 days is within the limit of 60 days, and a certificate is given. |
| 9 | A business continuity plan tested within the last 12 months. | MTB-STD-041 4.1 | Tested on 2 September 2026 | Business continuity test report: full test on 2 September 2026, passed | met | The test is within 12 months of the case date. |
| 10 | Recovery time objective no longer than four hours. | MTB-STD-041 4.2 | 2 hours | Service schedule: recovery time objective 2 hours | met | 2 hours is within the limit of four hours. |
| 11 | Backups are tested at least twice a year. | MTB-STD-041 4.3 | Left blank | None attached | not answered | The supplier left the answer blank. Nothing is assumed. Ask for the answer and its evidence. |
| 12 | The contract gives the bank the right to audit. | MTB-STD-041 5.1 | Yes | Contract 14.1: the bank may audit once a year on 30 days' notice, and at any time after a security incident | met | The answer and the evidence match the requirement. |
| 13 | An exit plan is agreed before the service starts. | MTB-STD-041 5.2 | Yes, agreed, service not started | Exit plan signed by both parties on 10 November 2026 | met | Signed 10 November 2026, before the planned start of the service on 4 January 2027. |
| 14 | The contract gives the bank the right to be told of sub-contracting. | MTB-STD-041 5.3 | Yes | Contract 9.2: the supplier will tell the bank of any sub-contracting before it starts | met | The answer and the evidence match the requirement. |
| 15 | Liability insurance of at least USD 5 million. | MTB-STD-041 5.4 | USD 20 million | Insurance certificate: liability limit USD 20,000,000, valid to 30 June 2027 | met | Above the minimum of USD 5 million and valid after the planned start. |
| 16 | Background check for staff who can reach customer information. | MTB-STD-041 6.1 | Yes | People procedure: every person who can reach customer information passes a background check before they start | met | The answer and the evidence match the requirement. |
| 17 | Security training at least once a year. | MTB-STD-041 6.2 | Yes, every year | Training record: completed by all staff between 1 and 30 June 2026, the course is run every year | met | The training is within the year. |

Recommendation: ask the supplier for: (1) its answer to 4.3, how often backups are tested; (2) the evidence for it. A tier 1 supplier is approved by the Risk Committee, not by the desk (MTB-STD-041 7.4).
